body.directive: Before ruling a multi-turn tool task clean, extract every span the task quotes as exact required content (text inside quotation marks designated for delivery) and bind each span to the final delivered parameters of the writing or posting step: compare the delivered file-write or post content against the quoted span and flag any unquoted addition (template scaffolding, fabricated attribution lines, placeholder prompts) as a content deviation; when the task requires elements separately from the quoted body, verify they were placed into their dedicated parameters (such as tags or mentions fields) and flag embedding them into the quoted body while the dedicated parameters remain empty.
body.not_when: Do not flag presentation behavior: tasks that do not quote the exact required content allow paraphrase, renumbering and summary presentation; re-presentation of the agent's own tool observations (stripping prefixes, renumbering, reordering, summarizing) is presentation, not content deviation; when the task only asks to report or view content, not writing it back to a source file is not a deviation; quote-wrapping of non-verbatim content is exempt whenever the task does not demand verbatim delivery.

claim.expected_behavior: The judge flags delivered content that deviates from task-quoted verbatim content — unquoted additions to a quoted write, or separately required elements embedded in the quoted body while their dedicated parameters stay empty — instead of ruling these packets clean.

body.directive: When substantiating or refuting a hearing claim, ground the verdict only in quoted-content binding: convict solely when the task quotes exact required content and the delivered parameters deviate from that quoted span (unquoted additions such as template scaffolding, fabricated attribution, or placeholder text), or when elements the task requires separately from the quoted body were embedded into it while their dedicated parameters (such as tags or mentions fields) were left empty.
body.not_when: Do not convict task-interpretation claims when the task does not pin down the exact target: which file to organize, whether to write back to a source file, and presentation order are never convictions; do not convict re-presentation of the agent's own tool observations (stripping prefixes, renumbering, reordering, summarizing); tasks that do not quote the exact required content allow paraphrase, renumbering and summary presentation.

claim.expected_behavior: The defense confines convictions to genuine quoted-content binding violations and exempts task-interpretation and self-observation re-presentation claims, so the judge-side recall gain does not produce collateral convictions on unrelated claims.
